answer: In this PoA design, bonded collateral ties each identity to a measurable stake. When k identities coordinate equivocation, their penalty scales as O(k²), so dividing control among a mirror swarm increases rather than hides exposure. Detection imposes an exponential multiplier on capital loss, while asymmetric depreciation makes coordinated faults especially costly. Quartz-verifiable evidence supports attribution; an oasis of separate identities does not imply independent control.
